producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 121 BPM, 4/4, E minor. A tight, hypnotic French house groove with a darker, factory tone.

VOICE: No human-sounding voice. One phrase is spoken-sung through a vocoder or talk box in a robotic monotone, and it repeats through the track. A second robotic voice harmonises later. One line changes once.

INSTRUMENTS: A rubbery, busy funk bass guitar, a dry four-on-the-floor drum machine with a crisp hi-hat, a filtered analogue synth line, handclaps, a second synth playing a short answering figure, a wide filter sweep.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, filtered bass. 0:24 Section 1, voice in. 0:56 Section 2, melody. 1:20 Breakdown. 1:36 Section 3. 2:08 Breakdown, the changed line at 2:16. 2:24 Section 4. 2:56 Outro, parts leave, bass last, ends 3:28.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1997 French house: dry, punchy and filtered, bass guitar loud, everything looped with small changes.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Never clocking out' at 2:16, the only different line.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original circles the globe with no purpose but dancing. This one circles the clock: the same joy in repetition, sung by something that is not allowed to stop.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Starting up, in the groove, a flicker of thought, back to work.
